faqs.question: Is Tokyo or Osaka better for first-time visitors to Japan?
faqs.answer: Both are excellent for first-timers, but they offer different experiences. Tokyo is the quintessential mega-city with skyscrapers, world-class museums, the best metro on Earth, and every cuisine imaginable. Osaka is smaller, friendlier, more food-focused, and easier to navigate on foot. Reddit conse

faqs.question: How far apart are Tokyo and Osaka?
faqs.answer: Tokyo and Osaka are approximately 500 km apart. The Shinkansen bullet train takes about 2 hours 22 minutes on the Nozomi and costs around 13,870 yen (about 93 USD) one way for a reserved seat. The Hikari takes about 2 hours 58 minutes and is covered by the Japan Rail Pass.

faqs.question: Is it worth visiting both Tokyo and Osaka?
faqs.answer: Absolutely. If you have 7 or more days in Japan, most travelers recommend splitting time between both cities. A common split is 4 days Tokyo plus 3 days Osaka with day trips to Kyoto and Nara. The cities complement each other perfectly. Flying into one and out of the other saves time and money on ba

faqs.question: Which is cheaper, Tokyo or Osaka?
faqs.answer: Osaka is noticeably cheaper. Mid-range hotels in Osaka run 7,000 to 14,000 yen per night vs 10,000 to 20,000 in Tokyo. Street food in Osaka is legendary and cheap. Transit costs are comparable, but Osaka compact layout means you spend less time and money getting around.

faqs.question: How many days do you need in Tokyo vs Osaka?
faqs.answer: For a first visit: minimum 3 full days in Tokyo (ideally 4 to 5) and 2 to 3 days in Osaka. Tokyo has virtually unlimited things to do. Osaka highlights can be covered in 2 to 3 days, but it also serves as an excellent base for day trips to Kyoto, Nara, Kobe, and even Hiroshima.

faqs.question: Is Osaka friendlier than Tokyo?
faqs.answer: Yes, this is one of the most consistent observations from travelers. Osakans are famously outgoing, humorous, and approachable compared to the more reserved Tokyoites. The Kansai culture values directness and warmth. Tokyo is polite and efficient; Osaka is warm and boisterous.

faqs.question: Should I visit Tokyo or Osaka first?
faqs.answer: Most itineraries start in Tokyo (closer to Narita/Haneda airports) and end in Osaka/Kansai, or vice versa. The key is flying into one city and out of the other to avoid backtracking. If you arrive at Narita or Haneda, start in Tokyo. If you fly into Kansai International, start in Osaka.
